rationale: Recurring noun on this page (lines 2, 31, 32-restored) for the duration of life allotted to a generation. = Sahidic ⲁϩⲉ 'lifetime, span of life.' Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ. Distinct from ⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'life' as the abstract principle; ⲁⲍⲉ is the measurable quantity of years.

Hapax in this corpus, line 18 (twice). Cosmological term designating the heavenly counterpart and earthly domain of each time-lord. Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲱⲗⲡ̄/ⲥⲗⲏⲡ 'share, allotment.' Confidence low; flag for parallels in subsequent kephalaia.

Lycopolitan plural of ⲣⲟⲙⲡⲉ 'year' (cf. accumulated ⲣⲙⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ). Standard collective form on this page (lines 3, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30) for the years over which the year-lords reign. ⲛⲣⲙⲡⲉⲟⲩⲉ ⲛⲛⲓⲍⲁⲉⲩⲉ 'the years of these last (people)' — present-day humans.
Lycopolitan plural of ⲉⲃⲟⲧ 'month' (Sah. ⲉⲃⲁⲧⲉ). Used here as the second time-division (line 12 sg. ⲡⲉⲃⲁⲧ; line 29 pl.) under the lord-of-the-month, structurally parallel to ⲣⲙⲡⲉⲩⲉ 'years.'

Lycopolitan plural with demonstrative ⲛⲓ-, on root ϩⲁⲏ 'last, end' (cf. ⲡⲓⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲍⲁⲉ 'this last bōlos' in glossary). Designates the present-day generations as opposed to ⲛⲓϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ 'the first generations.'

proposed_english: many in lifespan / abounding in life
rationale: Idiomatic phrase ⲣ̄- ('do/be') + ⲍⲁⲍ ('many,' = Sah. ϩⲁϩ) + ⲛ̄-ⲁⲍⲉ ('of lifespan'). Describes the long-lived condition of Adam, Sethel, and their successors. Standard Manichaean characterization of the antediluvian generations.

Lycopolitan plural of ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'father.' Distinct from accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'the Fathers' (Lyc. pl.); ⲁⲓⲉⲩⲧⲉ is the bare noun without article. Confidence moderate; the noun-reading is supported by the genitive prefix ⲛⲧⲁⲩ- 'their/of-them.'
Lycopolitan ordinal: ⲙⲁⲍ- (ordinal prefix) + ⲧⲟⲩ (= ϯⲟⲩ '5'). Pattern matches ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲁϣϩ 'seventh,' ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ 'third' already in vocabulary.
Coptic ⲥⲟⲩⲥⲟⲩ 'instant, moment, brief time' (Crum 369a). Smallest unit in the time-enumeration year/month/day/hour/moment. The fifth and shortest temporal lord.

Standard Coptic ⲥⲱⲛⲧ 'creation, that which is created' (Crum 345a). Used cosmologically: the powers receive authority 'from the beginning of the creation unto the end of the cosmos.' Distinct from ⲕⲱⲧ 'building/structure' and ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ 'molding.'

Coptic ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'birth, offspring' (Crum 187a). The verbal noun referring to children/descendants begotten under the dominion of each time-lord. Conceptually aligned with ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget' which appears throughout this passage.
Greek χρόνος with possessive prefix. Distinguished here from ⲕⲁⲓⲣⲟⲥ (appointed time): ⲭⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ designates duration/epoch. Used in pair with ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ for the long-extending early ages of humanity.
